'''Tom Weidig''' (born 9 December 1972) is a Luxembourgish politician.<ref name="tw1">{{cite web |title=Tom Weidig |url=https://www.vdl.lu/en/city/political-life/municipal-council/members/tom-weidig |website=Ville de Luxembourg |access-date=30 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He has served as a Member of the [[Chamber of Deputies (Luxembourg)|Chamber of Deputies]] from [[Centre (Chamber of Deputies of Luxembourg constituency)|Centre]] since 2023, as a representative of the right-wing [[Alternative Democratic Reform Party]] (ADR).<ref name=tw1 /> He supports the promotion of the [[Luxembourgish language]].<ref name="tw2">{{cite web |title=Tom Weidig |url=https://www.oecd-events.org/gpn2025/en/speaker/7feca5ab-52dd-ef11-88f8-6045bd89b60c/tom-weidig |website=OECD events |publisher=[[OECD]] |access-date=30 April 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2025, Weidig received a written warning from his party after he [[Facebook like button|liked a Facebook comment]] that was described as being anti-LGBTQ+.<ref name="javel">{{cite web |last1=Javel |first1=Florian |title=ADR warns MP Tom Weidig over homophobic social media ‘like’ |url=https://www.luxtimes.lu/luxembourg/adr-warns-mp-tom-weidig-over-homophobic-social-media-like/41793499.html |website=[[Luxembourg Times]] |access-date=30 April 2025 |date=18 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 18, 2025 |title='Red lines are being crossed', LSAP accuses ADR of tolerating far-right stance, demands party president step down |url=https://today.rtl.lu/news/luxembourg/lsap-accuses-adr-of-tolerating-far-right-stance-demands-party-president-step-down-2277933 |url-status=live |access-date=December 23, 2025 |website=today.rtl.lu}}</ref> He issued an apology, but also insisted his actions had been misunderstood.<ref name=javel />

== Early life and education ==
Weidig was born and brought up in [[Esch-sur-Alzette]].<ref name="welsch">{{cite web |last1=Welsch |first1=Annette |date=3 November 2023 |title=Tom Weidig: Der Mann, der gegen den Strom schwimmt |url=https://www.wort.lu/politik/tom-weidig-der-mann-der-gegen-den-strom-schwimmt/4618294.html |access-date=30 April 2025 |website=[[Luxemburger Wort]] |language=de-LU}}</ref> His parents were from [[Grevenmacher]].<ref name="welsch" /> As a teenager, he represented Luxembourg at the [[World Junior Chess Championship]].<ref name="welsch" /> He graduated from [[Imperial College London]] in 1996 with a [[Master of Science]] degree in Theoretical Physics, and earned his doctorate from [[Durham University]] in 1999.<ref name="tw1" /> He was then a [[postdoc]] at [[UMIST]], and in 2001 a visiting scholar at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]].<ref name="tw2" /> 

== Career ==
Weidig has worked in the finance and venture capital industries.<ref name="welsch" />

== Personal life and public image ==
Weidig, who developed a [[stutter]] in early childhood, has a strong interest in the science behind stuttering.<ref>{{cite web |title=People involved |url=https://www.bps2.com/home/people |website=BPS2 |access-date=30 April 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211230203/https://www.bps2.com/home/people |archive-date=11 December 2024}}</ref> He was a board member of the [[British Stammering Association]] from 1995 to 1999.<ref name=tw1 />

In a July 2026 Ilres poll, with 75% name recognition, Weidig ranked as the least popular of all Luxembourgish politicians tested, with an average score of 9.4%.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Xavier Bettel retains top spot in political popularity as Luc Frieden remains outside top ten |url=https://today.rtl.lu/news/luxembourg/xavier-bettel-retains-top-spot-in-political-popularity-as-luc-frieden-remains-outside-top-ten-1402397352 |date=7 July 2026 |access-date=7 July 2026 |website=RTL Today}}</ref>
